batches.objective: Resolve the remaining whole-process Vulkan preparation deficit after retaining source-bound entry-point reflection reuse.
batches.rationale: The pointer, test-isolation, and public-render batches passed in reports/maintenance/20260928-pointer-public. The 20261002 Vulkan preparation report shows a physical repeated-pipeline improvement from 59.83 to 40.10 ms, but unchanged UMAP complete-process latency did not improve. Package import in Vitest, device request, and queue submission account for larger observed differences than eight shader and pipeline calls.
batches.nextAction: Profile package loading inside the unchanged UMAP host, including Vite transformation versus direct Node import; inspect Vulkan device-request and queue-submission costs with native attribution. Choose one owned correction, measure compiler allocations if compilation is selected, and repeat the uninstrumented application comparison.
acceptance: Multiple pipelines and entry points, changed overrides, failures, cache hits and misses, and caller release preserve reflection, specialization, and diagnostic behavior; the 20261002 focused physical result is retained.
Native phase and allocation measurements establish any next mechanism; an unchanged physical Vulkan application comparison records full latency, memory, correctness, and pinned Dawn control.
batches.stopCondition: Retain or reject the candidate from complete application and regression evidence, with generated-SPIR-V execution left as the subsequent bounded investigation.
requiredEnvironment: Pinned Dawn control and unchanged UMAP application
